samples.summary: Whole-root JSON snapshot for `sheet` copies comment threads, contradicting the design doc's Non-Goal "Comments … deliberately not carried over"
samples.evidence: Spreadsheet comment threads live *inside* the Yorkie root: `packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:94` declares `comments?: { … }` per worksheet and seeds `comments: {}` at creation (line 147); `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1318,1366` reads `ws.comments`. `copyContent` for `JSON_ROOT_TYPES = ['sheet','slides','board']` assigns *every* root key onto the target, so a copied sheet inherits the source's comment threads (bodies, authors, mentions) — exactly what docs/design/document-copy.md's Non-Goals section and the service's own class doc say is not carried over. Note the inconsistency across types: the `doc` arm goes through `readDocsRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:427), which does NOT read `root.comments` (declared in packages/frontend/src/types/docs-document.ts:24), so docs copies drop comments while sheet copies keep them. Either the doc's Non-Goal or the sheet arm is wrong.

samples.summary: Unrelated extraction of `unwrapJson` into a new module that the feature never uses (scope creep, and the new code re-implements it anyway)
samples.evidence: The diff moves `unwrapJson` out of `slides-tree.ts` into `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts`, but grep across packages/backend shows `slides-tree.ts:27` is still the only importer — `document-copy.service.ts` does not use it; it hand-rolls `snapshotJsonRoot` (document-copy.service.ts:~205) with the same unwrap-string-layers logic (also duplicated by `normalizeSnapshot` in packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:96). So the extraction is a no-op refactor unrelated to "Make a copy", and the shared helper it creates is not the one the new code reuses.

samples.summary: Canonical subsystem docs not updated: `POST /documents/:id/copy` is absent from backend.md's Documents endpoint list and `copyDocument` from frontend.md's API-function table
samples.evidence: docs/design/backend.md:158-185 is an exhaustive per-endpoint reference for `/documents` (GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, plus the manager-gate note), and docs/design/frontend.md:428-434 tabulates every `api/documents.ts` function → method → path. The new endpoint and client function are only described in the new top-level document-copy.md, so the canonical subsystem docs now omit a document endpoint whose permission gate deliberately diverges from every other one — the single most important thing a reader of backend.md's access-model section would need.

samples.summary: `if (!JSON_ROOT_TYPES.has(type)) return;` silently no-ops for unknown types, diverging from the repo's "unknown document type throws" convention
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-doc-key.ts:8-11 states the convention explicitly: "Any new document type must be added here; an unknown type throws so the mistake surfaces at request time instead of silently falling through." `copyContent` instead treats every non-listed type as "no CRDT content", so a future ninth document type (or a typo'd type value) yields a successful-looking copy with empty content — the exact failure mode the rollback logic elsewhere in this file is designed to prevent.

samples.summary: `slides` bypasses the existing `readSlidesRoot`/`writeSlidesRoot` serializer that the v1 content endpoint uses, giving two divergent notions of a slides root copy
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:52-110 is the backend's canonical slides root read/write pair (used by the REST v1 content endpoint, with `meta` normalization and `guides` backfill). The copy service instead routes `slides` through the generic whole-root snapshot (JSON_ROOT_TYPES at document-copy.service.ts:27). The design doc justifies it (copies fields added later), but the result is two different slides-root write contracts in the same package; if the generic path is right, the doc should say why slides-tree stays the odd one out, or slides-tree's normalization is silently skipped on copy.

samples.summary: Goal "duplicates a document of any type with its full content" is not met for `doc`, by the doc's own admission
samples.evidence: document-copy.md's Goals claim full-content duplication for any type, while the same doc later concedes the `doc` arm "inherits their documented limitations (legacy header/footer shapes are not migrated; inline images are opaque attribute strings)" because it round-trips through `readDocsRoot`/`writeDocsRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:427,517 — an explicitly lossy, destructive-replace serializer). The Goal and the Proposal Details contradict each other; the Goal should be scoped, or the fidelity gap listed as a Non-Goal/known limitation rather than buried in prose.

finding.summary: Whole-root JSON snapshot for `sheet` copies comment threads, contradicting the design doc's Non-Goal "Comments … deliberately not carried over"
finding.evidence: Spreadsheet comment threads live *inside* the Yorkie root: `packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:94` declares `comments?: { … }` per worksheet and seeds `comments: {}` at creation (line 147); `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1318,1366` reads `ws.comments`. `copyContent` for `JSON_ROOT_TYPES = ['sheet','slides','board']` assigns *every* root key onto the target, so a copied sheet inherits the source's comment threads (bodies, authors, mentions) — exactly what docs/design/document-copy.md's Non-Goals section and the service's own class doc say is not carried over. Note the inconsistency across types: the `doc` arm goes through `readDocsRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:427), which does NOT read `root.comments` (declared in packages/frontend/src/types/docs-document.ts:24), so docs copies drop comments while sheet copies keep them. Either the doc's Non-Goal or the sheet arm is wrong.

verdict.reason: Verified in-tree. `copyContent` treats `sheet` (with `slides`/`board`) as a whole-root JSON snapshot and assigns every root key onto the new document (document-copy.service.ts:27, 176-198) with no key filtering. Sheet comment threads are stored inside that same Yorkie root — `Worksheet.comments?: { [threadId]: Thread }` (worksheet-document.ts:94-96), seeded at creation (line 147), reachable via `SpreadsheetDocument.sheets` (lines 115-119), and mutated/read live through the Yorkie proxy (yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:4-5,88-125; yorkie-store.ts:1318,1366). So a copied sheet inherits the source's comment threads, contradicting the explicit Non-Goal in docs/design/document-copy.md:32-35 ("Comments, share links, presence, and analytics are deliberately not carried over") and the service's own class doc (document-copy.service.ts:35-37). The claimed inconsistency is also real: readDocsRoot (docs-tree.ts:427-468) reads only content/pageSetup/stylesJson — grep for `comments` in that file returns no matches — so the `doc` arm drops comments while the `sheet` arm keeps them. Either the doc's Non-Goal or the sheet arm is wrong; that is a spec-conformance/Non-Goal violation, which is `major` and blocking under this lens.
